titulo: nVision, international trade fairs · Roger Avellana
descripcion: Case study: materials for nVision Systems’ international R&D trade fairs. Challenge, process, deliverables and results.
entradilla: nVision Systems presents its R&D work at international trade fairs, where each visitor spends only a few seconds at every booth. I designed the stand, roll-ups, technical brochures and presentations so that its technology could be understood from afar and convince up close.

resumen.reto: Every fair was prepared with different, highly technical materials. The stand didn’t explain what the company did, and the brochures were written for engineers, not for potential clients.
resumen.solucion: A reusable trade fair kit: a modular stand, roll-ups with one message each, technical brochures with two reading levels and a shared presentation template.
resumen.resultado: A stand that is recognizable at any fair and takes less time to prepare, plus materials the sales team also uses outside the fairs.

proceso.titulo: From the lab to the booth.
proceso.intro: Turning R&D into clear messages without losing rigor, with a system that worked for any fair and any country.

pasos.texto: Sessions with the R&D team to identify what each product does, who cares about it and what can be demonstrated at the fair.
One main message per piece, depending on distance: what you read at 5 meters, at 2 meters and in your hand.
Modular stand, roll-ups, technical brochures and infographics with the same grid and the same visual style.
Large-format print-ready artwork, language adaptations and a presentation template for the team.

entregables.titulo: A kit for any trade fair.
entregables.intro: The same pieces adapted to every event, every language and every stand size.

cifras.texto: international trade fairs in 4 countries with the same system
reading levels: at 5 meters, at 2 meters and in your hand
time to prepare the materials for each fair

testimonio.texto: Working with Roger on international trade fairs was key: complex technology turned into materials anyone could understand.
